summary: Indologist Helen Moore Johnson earned degrees from Missouri and Wisconsin and studied under Maurice Bloomfield at Johns Hopkins. She held posts at the University of Science and Arts of Oklahoma, Oxford College for Women, and Johns Hopkins University (1924–1936).

Helen Wang is a scholar of sinology, history and archaeology, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. She studied at SOAS University of London (ca. 1984–1988) and became Curator of East Asian Money at the British Museum around 1993.
Helena Blankleder is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Tibetology. She studied under traditional teachers Pema Wangyal Rinpoche and Jigme Khyentse Rinpoche, both attested in 1999.
Helena Michie studied at the University of Pennsylvania from around 1979 to 1984 and held a post at Rice University around 1990.

Helena Willman-Grabowska worked in Indology, linguistics, and Iranian and Central Asian studies. After studies in Bern, Lausanne, and Paris under Sylvain Lévi, Antoine Meillet, and others, she taught at Paris, the EPHE, and as professor at Jagiellonian University (1927–1948).

Helga Uebach was a scholar of Tibetology and Indology who completed her Ph.D. under Helmut Hoffmann at the University of Munich (ca. 1961–1967). In 1964, she served as an editorial consultant at the Bavarian Academy of Sciences and Humanities.
Linguist Hellfried Dahlmann held academic posts at the University of Marburg (ca. 1935–1953) and the University of Cologne (ca. 1953–1970).

Sinologist Hellmut Wilhelm earned his doctorate under Otto Franke at Humboldt University of Berlin. He taught German at Peking University (ca. 1933–1948) and held the chair of Sinology at the University of Washington from 1948 to 1971.

Hellmuth Hecker was a Buddhist studies scholar who studied at the University of Hamburg (earning a Ph.D. ca. 1948) and under Paul Debes. He served as a Referent at the University of Hamburg from around 1952 to 1988.

Helmer Smith worked in Indology, Buddhist studies, and linguistics, studying at Uppsala and under Johansson, Andersen, and Bloch. He served as Docent of Indology at Lund (1921–1935) and professor of Sanskrit and comparative linguistics at Uppsala (1936–1947).
Linguist Helmut Arntz studied under Hermann Hirt from around 1931 to 1934 and held a post at the University of Giessen from around 1935 to 1945.

Helmut Eimer was a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who completed his doctorate under Frank-Richard Hamm at the University of Bonn. He subsequently held a post at the University of Bonn from around 1975 to 2001.

Helmut Hoffmann specialized in Indology, Tibetology, and Buddhist studies, earning his Dr. phil. under Heinrich Lüders in Berlin. He served as professor at the University of Munich (1948–1968) and Indiana University Bloomington (1969–1980).

Helmut Krasser was a scholar of Buddhist studies, Indology, and Tibetology who completed his doctorate and habilitation at the University of Vienna. He worked at Vienna, the Austrian Academy of Sciences, and directed the Institute for the Cultural and Intellectual History of Asia.

Helmut Nespital was an Indologist and linguist who studied at Humboldt University and Charles University under Vincenc Pořízka. He held posts at Humboldt University, the University of Bamberg, and served as professor of Indology at the Free University of Berlin.

Helmut Rix was a linguist and Indologist who earned his Ph.D. at Heidelberg and habilitation at Tübingen under Karl Hoffmann. He served as a professor at the University of Regensburg (1966–1982) and the University of Freiburg (1982–1993).

Helmut Tauscher is a Tibetology and Buddhist studies scholar who earned his Dr. phil. under Ernst Steinkellner at the University of Vienna. He served as an assistant and associate professor at Vienna (1981–2015) and was Numata visiting professor at Leiden.

Helmut Uhlig was a scholar in Buddhist studies, history, and archaeology who studied at the University of Vienna. He taught at the Volkshochschule and served as director of Volkshochschule Tempelhof in 1956.

Helmuth Peter Holler was a scholar of religious studies and Indology who studied in Berlin and Kiel. He served as principal of Rajahmundry Seminary (1897–1900) and was founder, principal, and professor at Oriental University (ca. 1903–1925).

Helmuth von Glasenapp worked in Indology and religious and Buddhist studies, earning his doctorate under Hermann Jacobi at Bonn. He served as Privatdozent at Bonn and Berlin, before holding chairs at Königsberg (1928–1944) and Tübingen (1946–1959).
